question: How many tests burned Kapton, and in which investigations?
claim: 30 PSI tests used Kapton as the sample material: 29 in PSI-101 (SAME-R) and 1 in PSI-102 (SAME), both smoke tests in microgravity.
summary_student: Kapton shows up as the test material in 30 PSI tests. Almost all of them, 29, are in SAME-R (PSI-101) and 1 is in SAME (PSI-102). Both experiments studied the smoke a heated material gives off so that smoke detectors can be tested, not open flames.
summary_professional: Rows whose fuel/sample field reads Kapton: n = 30 tests, of which 29 are in PSI-101 (SAME-R, Experimental table_SAME-R.csv) and 1 in PSI-102 (SAME, Experimental table_SAME.csv). All rows are classified as phase smoke under microgravity, read from the Sample Type column. Neither table reports O2 or pressure, and no outcome is recorded for these rows.

params.sql: SELECT lower(replace(investigation, '-', '')) || '_kapton_tests' AS name, count(*) AS value, 'tests' AS unit, investigation, source_table, list(source_row ORDER BY source_row) AS source_rows, list(DISTINCT json_extract_string(field_sources, '$.fuel')) AS source_columns FROM tests WHERE fuel ILIKE '%kapton%' GROUP BY investigation, source_table ORDER BY investigation

method.formula: The values returned by the SQL query in params, one row per value, each with the source rows it used.

assumptions: A test is counted when its fuel or sample field, as written in the PSI table, contains the word Kapton (case-insensitive).
The question's word burned is read as tests that used Kapton as the sample; the tables classify these rows as smoke tests, not flame tests.
limitations: Covers only rows whose fuel or sample field names Kapton; rows that describe the same material with a different name are not counted.

The SAME and SAME-R tables give no O2 level and no pressure, so this finding says nothing about how Kapton behaves at any particular oxygen level or pressure, including the lunar base or pressurized rover atmospheres.
No outcome is recorded for these rows, so the finding does not say whether Kapton ignited, how much smoke it produced, or whether it is safe or unsafe.
All counted tests are in microgravity; the finding covers no Earth-gravity or partial-gravity Kapton tests.

chart.idea: Bar chart of the number of Kapton tests in PSI-101 (SAME-R) and PSI-102 (SAME).

graph.idea: Proof graph linking the finding to PSI-101 (SAME-R) and PSI-102 (SAME), their source tables, and the shared Kapton sample material.
